title: Alia Bhatt Picks Up the Rifle: 'Alpha' Storms In as the Spy Universe's First Female-Led War
excerpt: 75 million views in a day, a Kashmir-set assassin origin story, and a cameo bench stacked with Pathaan, Tiger and Kabir — YRF's 350-crore gamble lands worldwide July 3.
body:
A toddler is taken. A father who isn't really a father hands her a knife instead of a doll. And somewhere between the gunfire and the snow of a Kashmir monastery, a girl named **Sita** decides she'd rather rewrite the myth than wait around to be rescued. That's the pitch of **Alpha** — and on June 10, when Yash Raj Films finally let the teaser loose, the internet did the math in record time: **75 million views in 24 hours**, one of the biggest digital launches India has ever seen.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

This is the one the whole industry has been circling. **Alpha** is the seventh film in the YRF Spy Universe — the franchise that gave us *Ek Tha Tiger*, *War*, and *Pathaan* — but it's the first to put a woman, two women actually, at the dead center of the carnage. **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** headline. **Bobby Deol** plays the villain who made them. **Anil Kapoor** runs the spy agency from the shadows. And the budget, reportedly ₹350 crore, tells you exactly how seriously Aditya Chopra is taking this gamble.

> "What I loved most was that at the heart of it were two women leading all the action. We don't get to see that very often." — Alia Bhatt

Let's talk about the teaser, because it's a flex. Bhatt has never looked like this on screen — lean, feral, all coiled muscle and dead-eyed calm, throwing hands in tactical gear like she was born holding a rifle. Bobby Deol, gravel-voiced and terrifying, delivers a little sermon about predators and prey, and Bhatt's character quietly accepts her place as the wolf. It's gritty in a way the glossy *Pathaan*-era Spy Universe usually isn't. Directed by **Shiv Rawail** — the man behind the acclaimed Netflix series *The Railway Men*, making his feature debut — the film leans dark, and the visuals back it up: hand-to-hand combat shot tight, chase sequences across Mumbai, Kashmir, and Valladolid, Spain, and a color palette closer to a thriller than a popcorn spy romp.

The trailer, dropped a week later on June 17, finally gave Sharvari her entrance — and it's a doozy. Where Bhatt broods, Sharvari arrives loud, colorful, kinetic, and the two eventually stop fighting each other long enough to take aim at Deol's Fateh together. (YRF is being cagey about Sharvari's full arc, which usually means there's a twist worth protecting.) Then comes the closer everyone screenshotted: a figure in white at a monastery, green eyes glinting in the dark. **Hrithik Roshan**'s Major Kabir, back from *War*. The cameo bench, per the film's Wikipedia page, doesn't stop there — **Shah Rukh Khan**'s Pathaan, **Salman Khan**'s Tiger, **NTR Jr.**, and **John Abraham** all reportedly drop in. This isn't a film; it's a universe collecting interest.

What makes the marketing genius is the framing. Bhatt's character is named Sita, after her mother Janaki — a direct nod to the *Ramayana*'s abducted princess. Except this Sita doesn't pray for a rescue. She trains, she breaks, she turns on the man who built her. It's mythology weaponized, and it's a smart, slightly subversive hook for a culture that knows the original story in its bones.

The endorsements rolled in like a coronation. **SS Rajamouli**, **Shah Rukh Khan**, **Priyanka Chopra**, **Salman Khan**, **Katrina Kaif**, **Jr. NTR**, and **Vicky Kaushal** all publicly praised the teaser — and in case you needed proof of domestic bliss, **Ranbir Kapoor** showed up in a custom tee reading "My Wife's An Alpha." Subtle, the Bhatt-Kapoors are not.

**Where the diaspora comes in:** Alpha gets a worldwide theatrical release on **July 3, 2026**, which means NRIs in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia catch it the same weekend as Mumbai — no painful wait, no spoiler-dodging. YRF films almost always get wide overseas distribution (think AMC and Cineworld chains), and a Friday drop is built for diaspora date nights. The studio also engineered an open run: rival *Dhamaal 4* slid to July 17 and even Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey* releases later that month, leaving Alpha a clean two weeks to dominate.

Here's the take: female-led action in Bollywood has historically been handed a smaller budget and a quieter release. Alpha got ₹350 crore, the full Spy Universe cameo arsenal, and a marketing campaign built like a war. If it lands, it doesn't just open a sequel slate — it rewrites who gets to carry a blockbuster. And on the evidence of that teaser, Bhatt is more than ready to pick up the rifle.
